newsitem.title: UK: Uk's Littlewoods drops stores expansion plan - paper.
newsitem.headline: Uk's Littlewoods drops stores expansion plan - paper.

text.p: Liitlewoods, Britain's largest private company, is scrapping plans for a 135 million pound ($228 million) expansion of its department stores and the creation of 3,000 jobs to concentrate on home shopping, the Financial Times reported on Friday.
The move has prompted the departure of Bob Willet who has resigned as managing director of Littlewood's stores division in protest at the changes according to the newspaper.
The switch marks a radical change in business strategy six months after James Ross, former chief executive of Cable & Wireless was brought in to shake up the football pools-to-retailing group.
The Financial Times also said that the company is expected to announce the purchase of mail-order business Freemans from Sears Plc for close to 400 million pounds early next week.
